newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: American executives anti US policy on China - report.
newsitem.headline: American executives anti US policy on China - report.

text.p: Many American executives dealing with Asian countries are critical of U.S. government policy towards China, saying it interferes with business, Political & Economic Risk Consultancy (PERC) said.

Hong Kong-based PERC said in a report received by Reuters on Monday that a survey of business leaders in seven cities in the United States approved of U.S. foreign policy towards most Asian countries by a factor of two to one.
But, on China, the picture was reversed.

"In the case of China, from the perspective of the U.S. businessmen we surveyed, the consensus view was that politics has definitely interfered with their business in a negative way," the report said.

"This perception, together with the relatively negative evaluation of the overall quality of U.S. policy toward China, would seem to indicate that businessmen tend to blame Washington, rather than Beijing, for a large part of their difficulties," it added.
PERC said the survey was also critical of U.S. policy on Vietnam, but gave no details.
The report did not give details of the size of the sample for the survey.
